faqs.q: What are Oteco G-10-S and G-102-S wireline guides and BJ Roliguide parts?
faqs.a: They are complete six-roller wireline guides, nitrile rollers, shafts, bearings and spiders, plus replacement rollers and parts for BJ Roliguide units, all supplied by Oteco. The listing has 23 part numbers. The guide hangs from the derrick on an Oteco hanging assembly.

faqs.q: How do I decode Oteco wireline guide part numbers such as 431101, 431122 and 431560?
faqs.a: The 4311 numbers are G-10 parts: 431101 is the complete G-10-S guide and 431111 the roller assembly. The 4311 20s are G-102 parts, with 431122 the complete G-102S guide. The 4315 numbers are BJ Roliguide parts, and 431560 is the complete BJ roller assembly.

faqs.q: What is the difference between the Oteco G-10-S and G-102-S wireline guides?
faqs.a: The G-10-S takes wireline to 1-1/2" and uses 5" diameter rollers, while the G-102-S takes wireline to 2" and uses 4-1/2" diameter rollers. Both rollers are 4-7/8" wide, and each guide carries six nitrile rollers on sealed bearings in a cast spider frame.

faqs.q: Which Oteco roller do I order for a BJ Roliguide?
faqs.a: Oteco lists 431560 as the complete replacement roller assembly for a BJ Roliguide, with shaft and bearings, in nitrile rubber. The roller is 5-1/2" diameter and 3-15/32" wide, for wireline to 2", and a guide carries 8 of them. Shafts, bushings, bearings and lock nuts are also listed singly.

faqs.q: What are Oteco wireline guide rollers made from?
faqs.a: The rollers are moulded in nitrile (NBR) rubber, and the guide uses steel and ductile castings. Nitrile is the listed roller compound for the G-10, G-102 and BJ Roliguide. Each G-10 or G-102 guide carries six rollers on sealed bearings.

faqs.q: Which Oteco parts support and complete a G-10 or G-102 wireline guide?
faqs.a: The guide hangs from the derrick on an Oteco hanging assembly; see [Oteco wireline guide hanging assemblies](/p/oteco-wireline-guide-hanging-assemblies) for the GF series. At the drawworks the line is turned onto the drum by a turnback, see [the Oteco G-20 wireline turnback](/p/oteco-g-20-wireline-turnback). Spare shafts, bearings, sleeves and spider frames are listed in the size table.

faqs.q: How do I install and maintain rollers in an Oteco wireline guide?
faqs.a: Oteco Engineering Bulletin EB-005 covers installing rollers in the guide: torque the roller shaft nuts correctly, inspect the assembly and maintain the pulleys. We send the bulletin with the guide. Replacement shafts, bearings and spacer washers are listed singly.

faqs.q: Where is an Oteco G-10-S or G-102-S wireline guide used on a rig?
faqs.a: It guides the sand line or wireline coming off the drawworks and is hung in the derrick; Oteco lists hanging assemblies for beam and angle derricks. [rig hardware](/c/rig-hardware) at Indus Hydraulics includes the related turnback and hanging parts.

faqs.q: What maximum wireline size does the Oteco G-102-S guide take?
faqs.a: The G-102-S takes wireline to 2" maximum cable size and comes complete with its rollers as 431122. The G-10-S takes up to 1-1/2". The BJ Roliguide roller is also listed for wireline to 2". Check your line diameter against the size table before ordering.

faqs.q: Does Oteco list spare shafts and bearings for the G-10 wireline guide?
faqs.a: Yes. For the G-10, Oteco lists the roller shaft 301308, roller sleeve 301310, spacer washer 301312, shaft assembly with two bearings 431112, shaft only 431113, bearings in sets of 2 as 431114 and the spider frame casting 431118. Each is sold singly, so you can renew a worn part without the whole guide.

faqs.q: Where are Oteco wireline guides made?
faqs.a: Oteco wireline guides are made by Oteco Inc. in Houston, Texas, USA, and the country of origin is the United States. Indus Hydraulics is an authorised Oteco distributor for the Middle East and supplies the maker's documentation and part numbers.

faqs.q: Do you stock Oteco wireline guides, rollers and spares?
faqs.a: We keep Oteco wireline guides and rollers in stock at our warehouse in Dubai, UAE, and ship worldwide with the best lead times. Send the Oteco part number, or the guide model (G-10, G-102 or BJ Roliguide) and the part you need. [request a quote](/quote) to start.

faqs.q: What are Oteco G-20 wireline turnback assemblies?
faqs.a: Oteco G-20-H assemblies turn the sand line or wireline onto the drawworks drum. Sets are listed for the driller's and off-driller's side, complete, less base casting or less roller, with every wearing part listed singly. The listing has 19 part numbers.

faqs.q: How do I decode Oteco G-20 turnback part numbers such as 431201, 431202 and 431211?
faqs.a: 431201 is the complete G-20 turnback for both sides, 431202 is the driller's side only (right) and 431203 the opposite side (left). 431211 is the complete nitrile roller assembly. The special G-20-N parts are 431219 and 431225.

faqs.q: Which Oteco G-20 turnback assembly do I order for one side only?
faqs.a: Oteco 431202 is the driller's side only, right, and 431203 is the opposite driller's side, left. If you already have the base casting, 431205 is the set less roller and 431206 and 431207 are the right and left sides less roller. 431204 is the assembly less base casting, with 2 required for a complete set.

faqs.q: What roller and shaft parts are listed for the Oteco G-20 turnback?
faqs.a: Oteco lists the complete roller 431211 in nitrile, the G20 roller 431210, roller bearings in sets of 2 as 431216, the roller shaft 431217 and a coated shaft 431217CT, the shaft assembly with bearings 431218 and the U-bolts, set of 2, as 431215. The G-20 roller is 4-1/2" in diameter and 10-1/16" wide.

faqs.q: What is the Oteco G-20 turnback roller made from?
faqs.a: The G-20 roller is a nitrile (NBR) rubber compound roller; 431211 is the complete assembly. The frame uses steel and ductile castings. A coated shaft, 431217CT, is listed for the roller shaft.

faqs.q: What is the Oteco G-20-N turnback roller for National 1320 UE drawworks?
faqs.a: The G-20-N special roller, 431219, with its extension coupling shaft 431225, adapts the standard G-20 to National 1320 UE drawworks built in Japan. The roller is a nitrile rubber compound assembly. Send the drawworks model if you are unsure which version you need.

faqs.q: How should I maintain an Oteco G-20 turnback roller?
faqs.a: Oteco Engineering Bulletin EB-005 covers installing rollers: torque the roller shaft nuts correctly, inspect the assembly and maintain the pulleys. Bearings are listed in sets of 2, 431216, and the shaft separately, so a worn roller can be renewed without changing the frame.

faqs.q: Where does an Oteco G-20 wireline turnback sit on the rig?
faqs.a: The turnback sits at the drawworks and turns the sand line or wireline onto the drum. It works with a guide in the derrick: see [Oteco wireline guides and rollers](/p/oteco-wireline-guides-rollers) and [Oteco wireline guide hanging assemblies](/p/oteco-wireline-guide-hanging-assemblies). The listing is in [rig hardware](/c/rig-hardware).

faqs.q: Is there a maximum wireline size for the Oteco G-20 turnback?
faqs.a: The Oteco brochure gives the G-20 turnback roller as 4-1/2" diameter and 10-1/16" wide and lists no maximum wireline size for it, unlike the G-10 and G-102 guides. Send your line diameter and drawworks model and we confirm the fit with Oteco.

faqs.q: Where are Oteco G-20 wireline turnbacks made?
faqs.a: Oteco Inc. makes them in Houston, Texas, USA, and the country of origin is the United States. Indus Hydraulics is an authorised Oteco distributor for the Middle East. [contact us](/contact) for the maker's documentation and part numbers.

faqs.q: Do you stock Oteco G-20 wireline turnback assemblies and spares?
faqs.a: We keep Oteco G-20 wireline turnback assemblies in stock at our warehouse in Dubai, UAE, and ship worldwide with the best lead times. Send the Oteco part number, or the side, the parts needed and the drawworks model, and [request a quote](/quote).

faqs.q: How does the Oteco G-20 turnback differ from the G-10 and G-102 guides?
faqs.a: The G-20 turnback sits at the drawworks and turns the line onto the drum, with a 4-1/2" by 10-1/16" roller. The G-10 and G-102 guides hang in the derrick and carry six rollers each, each 4-7/8" wide. See [Oteco wireline guides and rollers](/p/oteco-wireline-guides-rollers).

faqs.q: What are Oteco wireline guide hanging assemblies?
faqs.a: Oteco hanging assemblies support the Oteco roller guide in beam and angle derricks using the triangular method. Each includes mounting brackets and hardware, 3/8" tri-wire cable, pulleys and a drop cable assembly, and uses three HF-4 hayfork pulleys. The listing has 13 part numbers.

faqs.q: How do I decode Oteco GF hanging assembly numbers such as GF-32 and 431932?
faqs.a: The GF number is the assembly model and the Oteco part number follows it: GF-32 is 431932, GF-33 is 431933, GF-34 is 431934, GF-36 is 431936 and GF-37 is 431937. They differ by mast type and bracket style.

faqs.q: Which Oteco GF hanging assembly fits an angle derrick and which a beam derrick?
faqs.a: The brochure lists GF-32 and GF-33 for angle masts, GF-32 for 6" × 5-1/2" × 3/8" angle with flush brackets and GF-33 for 6" to 8" angle with 3'-0" brackets. GF-34 and GF-36 are for beam masts, 8" × 10-3/4" and 12-1/4" × 12-3/4", and GF-37 has welded telescope brackets.

faqs.q: What bracket lengths do Oteco GF-33, GF-34 and GF-36 hanging assemblies have?
faqs.a: GF-33 has adjustable brackets 3 feet long, GF-34 has 4 feet 7 inches and GF-36 has 3 feet 9-3/4 inches, each with 5 adjustment holes 1-1/4" apart. GF-37 has telescope brackets with 5 adjustment holes 3" apart. Match them to the mast section.

faqs.q: What cable and fittings do Oteco wireline hanging assemblies use?
faqs.a: They use 3/8" tri-wire cable with pulleys, a drop cable assembly, thimbles and turnbuckles. Oteco lists thimbles for 3/8" cable (301721) and for 1/4" cable (303006), a 3/4" turnbuckle (431561) and a hayfork pulley (431926). The support line is not included.

faqs.q: Which Oteco guide does a GF hanging assembly support?
faqs.a: It supports the Oteco G-10 or G-102 roller guide; see [Oteco wireline guides and rollers](/p/oteco-wireline-guides-rollers) for the guides and rollers. At the drawworks, the line is turned by [the G-20 turnback](/p/oteco-g-20-wireline-turnback). Thimbles, turnbuckles and hayfork pulleys are listed as spares.

faqs.q: How do I install an Oteco wireline guide hanging assembly?
faqs.a: Each assembly uses three HF-4 hayfork pulleys and the support line is not included. Oteco Engineering Bulletin EB-005 covers installing the rollers, torquing the shaft nuts, inspecting the assembly and maintaining the pulleys. We send it with the guide.

faqs.q: When do rigs need an Oteco hanging assembly for the wireline guide?
faqs.a: Whenever a G-10 or G-102 roller guide has to be hung in a beam or angle derrick. the assemblies use the triangular method. See [rig hardware](/c/rig-hardware) for the related turnback and guide parts.

faqs.q: Does the Oteco hanging assembly include the support line?
faqs.a: No. Each Oteco assembly includes the mounting brackets and hardware, 3/8" tri-wire cable, pulleys and drop cable assembly, but the support line is not included. You need to supply that separately.

faqs.q: Are GF-31, GF-35 and GF-38 hanging assemblies also available from Oteco?
faqs.a: Oteco lists 431838 as GF-31, 431935 as GF-35 and 431938 as GF-38, plus 431931 as GF-331, but the brochure table shows details only for GF-32, GF-33, GF-34, GF-36 and GF-37. Send the mast type and size and we confirm the right assembly with Oteco.

faqs.q: Where are Oteco hanging assemblies made?
faqs.a: Oteco Inc. makes them in Houston, Texas, USA, and the country of origin is the United States. Indus Hydraulics is an authorised Oteco distributor for the Middle East. [contact us](/contact) for the maker's documentation.

faqs.q: Do you stock Oteco wireline guide hanging assemblies?
faqs.a: We keep Oteco wireline guide hanging assemblies in stock at our warehouse in Dubai, UAE, and ship worldwide with the best lead times. Send the Oteco part number, or the mast type (angle or beam), mast section size and guide model. [request a quote](/quote) to start.

faqs.q: What are Oteco impact box wrenches BW5063 to BW5250?
faqs.a: They are forged steel, six-point, straight-handle striking wrenches for flange studs, BOP and wellhead bolting on the rig. Each wrench is sized by the stud and the nut across flats. The range has 14 sizes for 5/8" to 2-1/2" studs.

faqs.q: How do I decode Oteco impact wrench numbers such as BW5150 and 425150?
faqs.a: The BW number gives the stud size in hundredths of an inch: BW5150 is for a 1-1/2" stud with a 2-3/8" nut, and its Oteco part number is 425150. BW5063 is for a 5/8" stud and BW5250 for a 2-1/2" stud.

faqs.q: Which Oteco impact box wrench fits a 1-1/2" stud?
faqs.a: BW5150, part 425150, fits a 1-1/2" stud and a 2-3/8" nut across flats. For a 1-3/4" stud use BW5175 with a 2-3/4" nut, and for a 2" stud use BW5200 with a 3-1/8" nut. Check the nut across flats before ordering.

faqs.q: What stud and nut sizes do Oteco impact box wrenches cover?
faqs.a: The 14 wrenches cover studs from 5/8" to 2-1/2" with nuts from 1-1/16" to 3-7/8" across flats, for example BW5088 for a 7/8" stud with a 1-7/16" nut and BW5250 for a 2-1/2" stud with a 3-7/8" nut.

faqs.q: What are Oteco impact box wrenches made from?
faqs.a: Oteco impact box wrenches are made from forged steel, and have a six-point box and a straight handle. They are striking wrenches, so they are built to take hammer blows on the striking face. The listing states no coating or other material grade.

faqs.q: Is there a safe way to use an Oteco impact box wrench?
faqs.a: Strike only on the striking face, keep the box fully seated on the nut and use the correct size. Never extend the handle.

faqs.q: How should an Oteco impact box wrench be used on BOP and wellhead studs?
faqs.a: Select the wrench by the stud size and nut across flats, seat the box fully on the nut and strike the striking face with a hammer. Do not extend the handle. Oteco lists wrenches for flange studs and BOP and wellhead bolting.

faqs.q: Where are Oteco impact box wrenches used?
faqs.a: They are used on the rig floor and wellsite for flange studs, BOP bolting and wellhead bolting. Six-point boxes grip the nut across the flats and stand up to striking. See [rig hardware](/c/rig-hardware) for other Oteco rig tools.

faqs.q: Which Oteco wrench do I need for 7/8" studs?
faqs.a: Use BW5088, Oteco part 425088, for 7/8" studs with 1-7/16" nuts across flats. The next size down is BW5075 for 3/4" studs with a 1-1/4" nut, and the next size up is BW5100 for a 1" stud with a 1-5/8" nut.

faqs.q: Does Oteco state a heat treatment or standard for the BW5063 to BW5250 wrenches?
faqs.a: No. The Oteco listing gives the wrenches as forged steel, six-point, straight handle, and states no heat-treatment grade, hardness or standard. If you need a specific requirement, send it with your [request a quote](/quote) and we ask Oteco.

faqs.q: Where are Oteco impact box wrenches made?
faqs.a: Oteco Inc. makes them in Houston, Texas, USA, and the country of origin is the United States. Indus Hydraulics is an authorised Oteco distributor for the Middle East. [contact us](/contact) for the maker's documentation.

faqs.q: Do you stock Oteco impact box wrenches?
faqs.a: We keep Oteco impact box wrenches in stock at our warehouse in Dubai, UAE, and ship worldwide with the best lead times. Send the stud size and nut across flats, or the Oteco part number from 425063 to 425250, and [request a quote](/quote).

faqs.q: What are Oteco No. 1, No. 2 and No. 3 roller chain connectors?
faqs.a: They are steel chain connectors that pull the two ends of a heavy roller chain together so the connecting link can be fitted. They are used on drawworks, rotary and pump drive chains and cover chain from 1-1/4" to 4". The listing has 3 part numbers.

faqs.q: How do I decode Oteco chain connector numbers 432101, 432201 and 432301?
faqs.a: The digits after 432 carry the connector size: 432101 is the Number 1 connector, 432201 the Number 2 and 432301 the Number 3. The connector size you need depends on the chain pitch.

faqs.q: Which Oteco chain connector do I order for 2-1/4" to 3" roller chain?
faqs.a: The Number 2 connector, 432201, covers roller chain 2-1/4" to 3" and API 3, 3-1/2 and 4. The Number 3, 432301, covers 1-1/4" to 3" and the same API sizes. Number 1, 432101, is for 1-1/4" to 2-1/4".

faqs.q: What are the dimensions and weights of Oteco chain connectors No. 1, 2 and 3?
faqs.a: No. 1 is A max. 3" and B 11", weighing 5.3 lb (2.4 kg). No. 2 is A max. 5" and B 25-1/4", weighing 24 lb (10.9 kg). No. 3 is A max. 8" and B 25-1/4", weighing 26 lb (11.8 kg).

faqs.q: What chain sizes does each Oteco chain connector cover?
faqs.a: Number 1 covers roller chain 1-1/4" to 2-1/4", Number 2 covers 2-1/4" to 3" and API 3, 3-1/2 and 4, and Number 3 covers 1-1/4" to 3" and API 3, 3-1/2 and 4. The connector size depends on the chain pitch, so measure the chain first.

faqs.q: What material are Oteco roller chain connectors made from?
faqs.a: The Oteco listing gives the chain connectors as steel. It states no grade or coating. They are mechanical tools that draw the chain ends together, so the ratings that matter are the chain size range and the connector dimensions.

faqs.q: What does an Oteco chain connector do with the connecting link?
faqs.a: It pulls the two ends of the chain together so the connecting link can be fitted, which is the job on drawworks, rotary and pump drive chains. The link itself is not part of this listing. Send the chain size and we confirm the connector.

faqs.q: How do I choose between Oteco No. 2 and No. 3 chain connectors for API chain?
faqs.a: Both cover API 3, 3-1/2 and 4 chain. The Number 2 weighs 24 lb (10.9 kg) with A max. 5", and the Number 3 weighs 26 lb (11.8 kg) with A max. 8". Pick by the chain pitch and the opening you need.

faqs.q: When do rigs use an Oteco chain connector?
faqs.a: When a heavy drawworks, rotary table or pump drive chain has to be joined, replaced or shortened. The connector draws the chain ends together so the connecting link can be fitted. It belongs with the other [rig hardware](/c/rig-hardware) items.

faqs.q: Where are Oteco roller chain connectors made?
faqs.a: Oteco Inc. makes them in Houston, Texas, USA, and the country of origin is the United States. Indus Hydraulics is an authorised Oteco distributor for the Middle East. [contact us](/contact) for documentation.

faqs.q: Do you stock Oteco roller chain connectors?
faqs.a: We keep Oteco roller chain connectors in stock at our warehouse in Dubai, UAE, and ship worldwide with the best lead times. Send the chain size or API number and the connector number you want, and [request a quote](/quote).

faqs.q: Does Oteco publish an equivalent for its chain connectors?
faqs.a: No. Oteco lists the connectors by its own numbers 432101, 432201 and 432301 and publishes no interchange with other makers. Send the chain size and application and we confirm the Oteco connector.

faqs.q: What are Oteco shock pads for jack-up rig jacking systems?
faqs.a: Oteco shock pads cushion the jacking system of offshore jack-up rigs. Each pad is specially formulated rubber moulded between layers of corrosion-resistant steel plate, and every pad is tested under load before it ships.

faqs.q: What size are Oteco jack-up shock pads?
faqs.a: They are made to order, so there is no standard size. Send the drawing or the existing pad's dimensions, the design load and deflection, the number of plates and any fixing holes, and we return Oteco's quotation and lead time.

faqs.q: What information do I need to send to order an Oteco jack-up shock pad?
faqs.a: Send the drawing or the existing pad's dimensions, the design load and deflection, the number of plates and any fixing holes. We pass it to Oteco and return the quotation and the lead time. [request a quote](/quote) with the details.

faqs.q: Are Oteco jack-up shock pads load tested?
faqs.a: Yes. Oteco tests every shock pad under load before it ships. The listing gives no rated load, because each pad is built to the design load and deflection you specify.

faqs.q: What are Oteco jack-up shock pads made from?
faqs.a: Each pad is a laminate: specially formulated rubber moulded between layers of corrosion-resistant steel plate. The number of plates is set by your drawing. The listing does not name the rubber compound.

faqs.q: Can Oteco make a shock pad to replace an existing jacking pad?
faqs.a: Yes, shock pads are made to order from a drawing or from the existing pad's dimensions. Send the measurements, design load, deflection, plate count and fixing holes. Oteco then quotes the pad and the lead time.

faqs.q: How do I specify an Oteco shock pad for a jack-up jacking system?
faqs.a: Give the design load and deflection, the number of plates, the overall dimensions and any fixing holes, or send the drawing. Oteco moulds the rubber between corrosion-resistant steel plates and load tests the finished pad.

faqs.q: Where are Oteco shock pads used on a jack-up rig?
faqs.a: They are used in the jacking system of offshore jack-up rigs, where they cushion shock loads. They are one of the made-to-order items in the [rig hardware](/c/rig-hardware) range.

faqs.q: Where are Oteco jack-up shock pads made?
faqs.a: Oteco Inc. makes them in Houston, Texas, USA, and the country of origin is the United States. Indus Hydraulics is an authorised Oteco distributor for the Middle East and supplies the maker's documentation. [contact us](/contact) to discuss a pad.

faqs.q: Do you stock Oteco shock pads and how do I order one?
faqs.a: We keep Oteco rig hardware in stock at our warehouse in Dubai, UAE, and ship worldwide with the best lead times; shock pads are made to your drawing, so they are quoted per order. Send the drawing or dimensions, design load and deflection, plate count and fixing holes, and [request a quote](/quote).

faqs.q: Does Oteco publish a shock pad equivalent to another make?
faqs.a: No. Oteco makes the pad to your drawing or the existing pad's dimensions and publishes no interchange with other makers. Send the drawing and we obtain the quotation.

faqs.q: Is there a part number for an Oteco jack-up shock pad?
faqs.a: No standard part number is listed, because the pad is made to order. Send the drawing or dimensions and Oteco quotes the pad and lead time. Our listing code is IH-OTC-SHOCK-PAD.
